problem: Matching B input in g518 waited 1468.149ms for the service response despite 151.812ms native apply. The inner worker profile cannot explain the outer service response path. Timer lateness of 1299.451ms and GC/runnable observations are correlated, not proof of the whole cause.
changes: One zeroed ACK buffer belongs to each serial service connection, removing per-response buffer allocation. Input order, exact acknowledgements and fail-closed retirement remain unchanged.
The outer local IPC profile separates journal read, handling/serialization, native writer admission, submission-to-app-read, and remaining decode using same-host QPC.

g520 stamps pinned response bytes after writer mutex admission and event/pinning setup immediately before WriteFile. serviceNativeWrite distinguishes that observation from a generic io.Writer fallback.
Invalid suffix offsets and expired writes are rejected. A deadline is rechecked after stamping and before native submission; failed or short writes are not retried.

outerMicros.0: Zero; there is no distinct outer phase here.
outerMicros.1: App request write submission to journal request read completion.
outerMicros.2: Journal read completion through handling to reply serialization ready.
outerMicros.3: Reply-ready to native WriteFile submission point, including writer admission and event/pinning setup.
outerMicros.4: Native submission point to app first positive Read return; includes pipe delivery and app scheduling/resumption.

interpretation: Phases 3 and 4 identify native admission/post-submission only with serviceNativeWrite=true. No raw timestamp is exported. Ordered timestamps and a 120-second maximum window are validated only after sequence/op match. Outer spans include and overlap inner native-child spans: never add the two profiles. A native submission timestamp is not Write completion or kernel arrival.

benchmark.scope: Serialization into io.Discard on AMD Ryzen 5 7430U, Go 1.27.3 windows/amd64; not a native-pipe or physical crossing latency benchmark.
benchmark.conditionalBenefit: At 1000 service ACKs/second, this site saves 1000 allocations and 144000 allocated bytes/second. This does not establish that allocation caused the observed 1.47-second stall.

validation: Five full suites passed: inputworker, handoff, productlog, residentagent, localapi, count=1.
go vet passed for the same five packages.
Selected native submission, service IPC and buffer tests passed under -race in inputworker/handoff.
Actual Windows pipe test holds writer admission for 20ms and verifies it remains outside the post-submission phase.
Expired/invalid submission and orphan native-write metadata tests passed; git diff --check passed.
wire: Profiled local ACK suffix is 68 bytes (g518 used 44); no extra request, ACK, network round trip or I/O is added. Peer network protocol is unchanged. Matching application/protected-service images must be installed together.
rollout: g519 was built but not installed. Package g520 only from committed source. Preserve g518 evidence, install g520 on A and B and connect by CLI; record verified installation separately.
rollback: Keep prior generation artifacts. If g520 regresses, use its installer/update flow to restore matching prior app/service images; do not mix local wire generations or bypass retirement confirmation.
remainingRisk: Pipe delivery versus app scheduling remains ambiguous within phase 4. No physical latency improvement, long-term stability or elimination of the g518 stall is claimed before new user crossings.
apiDBRunner: Optional local diagnostic metadata extended; no external API, DB, dependency, GitHub runner or repository hygiene rule changes. No remote push or public release.
